chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibrahim ibn 'Uqbah from Muhammad ibn Muyassir from his father from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He who looks at the price of his goods while they are being weighed will not succeed.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of not watching the price while goods are being weighed in Islamic trade ethics?
ai.summary: In the context of Imam al-Sadiq’s commercial jurisprudence, this narration warns against the psychological state of anxiety during weighing, which can lead to hasty decisions or hidden defects in goods. It underscores the Shia ethical principle that spiritual success (falah) is tied to inner tranquility and divine trust (tawakkul) rather than mere transactional efficiency. This teaching aligns with the broader tradition of integrating spiritual mindfulness into daily economic activities.
